# Abstract

This project creates a rock-paper-scissors game, where the user plays against the computer. The user would play a move (rock, paper, scissors), the computer would play a move, and then the two would be compared. To accomplish this objective, the project delves into the intricacies of gesture recognition by using a series of LiDAR sensors to identify the user’s gesture of rock, paper, or scissors, and uses an LCD screen to communicate with the user.

First, a user would press a button to start a game. Then, the first round would start. The user plays their move, and so does the computer, which is displayed on the LCD. Then, the LCD displays if the user has won, lost, or tied. And finally, the user is given an option to move onto the next round, which would likely be more difficult.
